findings.title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific restrictions
findings.description: `canView(client)` returns true for an all-clients VIEW grant before evaluating the client’s own resource. A client-specific denial therefore cannot restrict that grant. `ClientsResource.getClients()` also uses parameterless `canView()` to bypass individual checks. Preserve role-based overrides, but evaluate fine-grained permissions against each client before exposing it. Add tests covering global grants with client-specific denials.

findings.title: MANAGE grants cannot list clients or client scopes
findings.description: Parameterless `canView()` recognizes VIEW but not MANAGE. Consequently, an administrator with only an all-clients MANAGE permission can create clients but fails inherited listing checks without an additional query role. Client-scope listing similarly fails despite `canManageClientScopes()` succeeding. Include MANAGE in the appropriate view/list checks and test without preassigned query roles; the current fixture’s QUERY_USERS role masks the client-listing failure.

findings.title: Permission enumeration does not return client IDs
findings.description: `findByType(..., "Clients", ...)` misses individual resources because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` never assigns their type. Meanwhile, the all-clients resource has that type, so a matching grant adds the literal `"Clients"` rather than actual client IDs. Enumerate real clients and evaluate their effective permission, or explicitly distinguish and expand the aggregate resource. Add coverage for both individual and all-clients grants.
